causal.donor_weights@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each bar is the mean weight of a donor in the synthetic copy of the treated unit. The line is the 90% interval. The weights are positive and add up to 1. geo_03: 3 donors have a weight of 5% or more, the largest are geo_00 (39%), geo_04 (30%) and geo_06 (17%). The typical difference before the start (RMSE) is 2.1. geo_07: 3 donors have a weight of 5% or more, the largest are geo_02 (42%), geo_06 (27%) and geo_09 (17%). The typical difference before the start (RMSE) is 3.4.
causal.donor_weights@1.0.0.title: Donor weights

causal.event_study@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each dot is the median effect in a period before or after the start, and the line is its 90% interval. Period -1 is the reference, so its effect is 0. The dashed red line marks the start. The average effect after the start is +3.61 (90% interval 3.26 to 3.96). There is no sign of different trends before the start. The first and the last dots include all the periods outside the window.
causal.event_study@1.0.0.title: Effect by period since the start

causal.impact@1.0.0.caption_plain: The line is the actual value. The dashed line and the band are the median and the 90% interval of the value without the intervention. The red line marks the start (2024-06-09) and the dashed red line the end (2024-06-30). In the effect window the total effect is +27.9 units sold (90% interval 18.5 to 36.4). This is +7% of the value without the intervention. The probability that the effect is above zero is 100%.
causal.impact@1.0.0.title: Effect of the intervention

causal.pre_fit@1.0.0.caption_plain: The dots are the actual values before the start (summed over 2 units). The line and the band are the median and the 90% interval of the model without the intervention. The typical difference (RMSE) is 1.94 units sold and the mean percentage error (MAPE) is 1%. 100% of the actual values are inside the band. The model follows the period before the start.
causal.pre_fit@1.0.0.title: Fit before the intervention

core.calibration@1.0.0.caption_plain: The line is the share of the 200 observations of y below each PIT value minus the share that a calibrated model gives. The band is where the line stays with probability 95% when the model is calibrated. The line goes outside the band, so the model is not calibrated. Too many observations are in the tails. The intervals are too narrow.

spec.title: PIT-ECDF difference of y (95% simultaneous envelope)

core.calibration@1.0.0.title: Calibration

core.confusion@1.0.0.caption_plain: The matrix counts the 300 observations of p by the observed class (rows) and the predicted class (columns). A case is positive (churn = 1) when the predicted probability is 0.432 or more. Accuracy 76%, precision 67%, recall (sensitivity) 73%, specificity 78%, F1 0.70. The threshold gives the largest difference between the true positive rate and the false positive rate.
core.confusion@1.0.0.title: Confusion matrix

core.convergence@1.0.0.caption_plain: 4 of 6 parameters have not converged (R-hat more than 1.01 or fewer than 200 effective samples), for example beta[tv], alpha[east], sigma. Before you trust the results, run the sampler longer, increase the tuning or reparameterise the model. There were 3 divergent transitions. The estimates can be biased.
core.convergence@1.0.0.title: Sampler convergence

core.counterfactual@1.0.0.caption_plain: The scenario changes total revenue by 184 (90% interval 139 to 251) compared with the baseline. Probability of an increase: 100%.
core.counterfactual@1.0.0.title: Scenario vs baseline

core.data_overview@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each panel shows one variable over week, with one line for each geo. The values show the sum over channel. spend has the most missing values (3% overall). The groups (geo) have from 19 to 20 observed values of revenue.
core.data_overview@1.0.0.title: Data overview

core.decision_distribution@1.0.0.caption_plain: shift_tv is the best option with probability 50%. Its expected objective is 0.92 (90% interval -0.56 to 2.58).
core.decision_distribution@1.0.0.title: Decision outcome

core.decomposition@1.0.0.caption_plain: For the full period, the outcome divides into: baseline 94%, tv 5%, search 2%. The values show the sum over geo.
core.decomposition@1.0.0.title: Decomposition

core.energy@1.0.0.caption_plain: The grey histogram is the energy of the sampler. The blue histogram is the change of energy from one draw to the next. When the blue histogram is much narrower than the grey one, the sampler does not explore the tails well. E-BFMI is from 0.19 to 2.09. 1 of 2 chains has an E-BFMI below 0.3 (chain 1). Do not trust the tails of the results. Change the parameterisation of the model or make the priors narrower.
core.energy@1.0.0.title: Sampler energy

core.fit_vs_actual@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each dot compares an actual value of revenue with the prediction of the model. Dots on the dashed line are perfect predictions. The model explains 52% of the variation (R² = 0.52) with a typical error of 4% (MAPE).
core.fit_vs_actual@1.0.0.title: Predicted vs actual

core.loo_pit@1.0.0.caption_plain: The left plot shows the LOO-PIT values of y: the line is the share of the 40 observations below each value minus the share for a calibrated model. Each observation is predicted by the model without that observation. The line stays inside the band: no sign of bad calibration. The right plot shows the Pareto k of each of the 40 observations. 1 observation (2%) has k above 0.7. The largest k is at the observation 7. For these observations, the leave-one-out estimate is not reliable, because each one has a large effect on the model. Do a check of these observations, or use a more robust model.
core.loo_pit@1.0.0.title: LOO-PIT and Pareto k

core.loss_curve@1.0.0.caption_plain: The light line is the value of negative ELBO at each step and the dark line is its moving average over 40 steps (fit_history). The moving average went from 21.3k to 425. In the last 10% of the steps it changed by -2%. The loss still goes down at the end. More steps can improve the fit. The y axis has a log scale.
core.loss_curve@1.0.0.title: Loss curve

core.model_comparison@1.0.0.caption_plain: unbiased has the best expected predictive accuracy (waic). biased is 32.3 ± 0.0 elpd worse: a clear difference. WAIC comes from the stored log-likelihood. Use PSIS-LOO when it is available.
core.model_comparison@1.0.0.title: Model comparison

core.pair@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each small plot shows the draws of two parameters; the diagonal shows the histogram of each parameter (5 parameters, 240 of 240 draws). The strongest correlation is between alpha[north] and beta[search] (r = -0.12). The red points are the 3 divergent transitions. If they gather in one corner, the sampler cannot reach that region (for example a funnel).
core.pair@1.0.0.title: Pair plot

core.posterior_forest@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each row is a model parameter. The dot is the posterior median. The thick bar is the central 50% interval. The thin line is the 94% highest-density interval. 6 of 6 intervals do not include zero.
core.posterior_forest@1.0.0.title: Posterior forest

core.ppc@1.0.0.caption_plain: 100% of the observations of revenue are in the 90% predictive interval of the model (ideal: about 90%). Very few observations are in the tails. The intervals are possibly too wide.
core.ppc@1.0.0.title: Posterior predictive check

core.ppc_fan@1.0.0.caption_plain: The line is the median estimate of revenue from the model. The shaded bands are the 50% and 90% intervals. The dots are the actual values. The dashed line marks where the training data ends.
core.ppc_fan@1.0.0.title: Fit and forecast

core.prior_posterior@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each panel shows the prior (grey) and the posterior (blue) of one parameter. The panels are sorted by how far the data moved the parameter. beta[tv] moved most: its mean changed by 2.15 prior standard deviations. Overlap: beta[tv] 43%, beta[search] 51%, sigma 21%, alpha[east] 27%, alpha[north] 28%, alpha[south] 32%.
core.prior_posterior@1.0.0.title: Prior and posterior

core.prior_predictive@1.0.0.caption_plain: The grey curves are datasets of revenue that the model can make before it sees data. The black curve is your data. Your data should look similar to the grey curves. 100% of the observations are in the prior 90% range.

vconcat.title: Prior predictive revenue over week (mean over geo)

core.prior_predictive@1.0.0.title: Prior predictive check

core.rank_matrix@1.0.0.caption_plain: Ranks of effect over the 8 levels of school (240 draws from posterior; rank 1 is the largest value). A has the best expected rank (1.8) and is first in 49% of the draws. It is above G with probability 83%.

hconcat.title: Rank of each school (sorted by expected rank)
Probability that the row is above the column

core.rank_matrix@1.0.0.title: Rank matrix

core.residuals_over_time@1.0.0.caption_plain: Residuals are actual minus predicted revenue. They should stay near zero. There is no important average bias.
core.residuals_over_time@1.0.0.title: Residuals over time

core.ridge@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each curve shows the possible values of effect for one school (8 levels, from posterior). The dot is the mean and the bar is the 94% highest-density interval. The top row is A (mean 14.2) and the bottom row is E (mean 3.83). The intervals of 7 of the 7 pairs of neighbouring rows overlap, so the order of those rows is not certain.
core.ridge@1.0.0.title: Ridgeline

core.roc_pr@1.0.0.caption_plain: The left plot shows the true positive rate against the false positive rate of p at each threshold. The right plot shows the precision against the recall. The AUC is 0.823: the model separates the classes well. 38% of the 300 observations are positive (churn = 1), so a model without skill has a precision of 0.38 (the dashed line). Over 100 draws, the 90% interval of the AUC is 0.806 to 0.828.
core.roc_pr@1.0.0.title: ROC and precision-recall curves

core.state_sequence@1.0.0.caption_plain: The coloured areas show the probability of each of the 2 states of state_prob (posterior) at each time. The most likely state changes 4 times; share of time as the most likely state: calm 70%, volatile 30%. At 11% of the times no state has a probability of 80% or more, so the state there is not certain.

vconcat.title: Observed, coloured by most likely state

core.state_sequence@1.0.0.title: State sequence

ml.confusion_epochs@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each matrix counts the validation images by the true class (rows) and the predicted class (columns) at one epoch, for 3 classes. Each row shows the share of the images of a true class. The validation accuracy is 60% at epoch 1, 100% at the best epoch (7) and 95% at epoch 10. The plot shows 6 of the 10 kept epochs.
ml.confusion_epochs@1.0.0.title: Confusion matrix over epochs

ml.feature_importance@1.0.0.caption_plain: The plot shows all 5 features. The model uses price most. It has 42% of the total importance. Importances show what the model uses. They do not show cause and effect.
ml.feature_importance@1.0.0.title: Feature importance

ml.misclassified@1.0.0.caption_plain: 17 of 60 validation images are wrong at epoch 7. The grid shows 12 of them, in order of the probability of the wrong class. Each title gives the true class, the predicted class and its probability. The mean probability of the true class for these images is 0.25. The plot shows 12 of the 17 wrong images.
ml.misclassified@1.0.0.title: Wrong validation images

ml.training_curves@1.0.0.caption_plain: The plot shows loss and accuracy at each step of the training, with one line for each split: train and val. The dark line of train is the moving average over 8 points. The light line is the value of each batch. The best validation loss is 0.23 at step 280. The best validation accuracy is 98% at step 280. The validation loss goes up while the training loss goes down: the model starts to overfit. The model keeps the weights of epoch 7.
ml.training_curves@1.0.0.title: Training curves

mmm.adstock@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each line shows the share of the effect of one unit of spend that comes 0, 1, 2 or more weeks after the spend. The shaded area is the 90% interval. tv has the longest carry-over. On average, its effect comes 1.87 weeks after the spend (90% interval 1.51 to 2.3). search has the shortest carry-over: 85% of its effect comes in the week of the spend.

vconcat.title: Share of the effect in each period

mmm.adstock@1.0.0.title: Carry-over of the effect

mmm.budget_plans@1.0.0.caption_plain: plan_b is expected to deliver 26.2 (3%) more outcome than current (90% interval -15.9 to 66.6). The probability that it is better: 84%.
mmm.budget_plans@1.0.0.title: Budget plan comparison

mmm.cross_effects@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each row is the change in the target outcome that goes with a rise of one unit in the source outcome. The lines are 90% intervals. The model measures an association, not a proof of cause. For 1 of 2 pairs, the interval does not include zero: premium to basic (+0.26).

x.title: effect (target units per unit of source)

spec.title: Effect of one outcome on another

mmm.cross_effects@1.0.0.title: Effects between outcomes

mmm.decomposition@1.0.0.caption_plain: For the full period, the outcome divides into: baseline 94%, tv 5%, search 2%. The values show the sum over geo.
mmm.decomposition@1.0.0.title: Contribution by component

mmm.effectiveness@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each line is the KPI that one unit of spend brings in each period, at the average spend level. The shaded area is the 90% interval. The effect of tv went from 2 to 1.45 (−28%) and was highest at 2024-01-28. The effect of search and social does not change over time (not shown).
mmm.effectiveness@1.0.0.title: Effect of spend over time

mmm.lift_tests@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each test has two rows. The black row is the result of the test (± 1.96 standard errors). The blue row is the 90% interval of the model for the same channel, period and market. The model does not agree with 1 of 4 tests: lift_1. For lift_1, the model gives 140 and the test gave 80. Look at the period and the market of the test, then look at the prior of the channel.
mmm.lift_tests@1.0.0.title: Lift tests and the model

mmm.marginal_cost@1.0.0.caption_plain: The cost per extra unit of response at each spend level in each channel. The shaded area is the 90% interval. At current spend, the cheapest next unit comes from tv (2.26).
mmm.marginal_cost@1.0.0.title: Marginal cost

mmm.mediation@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each bar divides the effect of a channel into its direct part and the parts that go through each mediator. The lines are 90% intervals. tv has the largest share through the mediators: 76% (68% to 84%). The largest mediated path is tv through awareness (310). The intervals of social through visits and social through awareness include zero.

x.title: share of the effect through mediators

mmm.mediation@1.0.0.title: Direct and mediated effects

mmm.prior_beliefs@1.0.0.caption_plain: Before the model sees the KPI, it puts the value of each channel on the black line (90% of the prior) and mostly in the dark bar (50%). The tick is at the median. The light band is the range that you gave. tv: 88% of the prior is in your range (you said 80%); search: 94% of the prior is in your range (you said 90%); baseline: 94% of the prior is in your range (you said 80%).
mmm.prior_beliefs@1.0.0.title: Your beliefs and the priors

mmm.response_curves@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each curve shows the expected response for each level of spend in a channel. The shaded area is the 90% interval. A steeper curve returns more for each extra unit of spend. A curve that becomes flat shows that the channel is near saturation. At current spend (diamonds), tv is closest to saturation. An extra unit there returns 29% of the return at its steepest point.
mmm.response_curves@1.0.0.title: Response curves

mmm.roi@1.0.0.caption_plain: ROI is the KPI that a channel brings for each unit of its current spend. Marginal ROI is the KPI that the next unit of spend brings. The lines are 90% intervals. search has the highest ROI (2.07). The ROI of social is below the break-even point (1) for all of the interval. In tv, the next unit of spend returns less than it costs. The next unit of spend returns most in search (marginal ROI 1.39, from the marginal_cost group).

x.title: marginal ROI (KPI per unit of spend)

mmm.roi@1.0.0.title: ROI and marginal ROI

mmm.spend_effect@1.0.0.caption_plain: For each channel, the grey bar is its share of the media spend and the blue bar is its share of the effect of all channels, with a 90% interval. A channel with a larger share of effect than of spend returns more than the average channel. search gets 20% of the spend and brings 29% of the effect. social gets 27% of the spend but brings only 10% of the effect.
mmm.spend_effect@1.0.0.title: Share of spend and share of effect

mmm.waterfall@1.0.0.caption_plain: The bars add up, from left to right, to the total of 5.76k over the period. Each line is the 90% interval of one step. The baseline parts give 81%. Of the channels, tv gives the most (11%).
mmm.waterfall@1.0.0.title: Contribution waterfall

net.graph@1.0.0.caption_plain: The network has 18 nodes (node). It shows tie_prob (the posterior mean of 60 draws) as an undirected graph. The graph draws the 33 links with tie_prob > 0.5. Thicker lines are stronger links. The node positions are the posterior mean of position. Point at the middle of a link to see the share of draws above the threshold (median 100%). The matrix shows every pair of nodes. Nodes that link to each other are next to each other in the order. The colours of the nodes show node_group. Dotted lines and open squares show the links in tie, for comparison.
net.graph@1.0.0.title: Network of tie_prob

sci.area_map@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each panel colours the 30 areas by one value of rr, from 120 draws of the posterior. The observed panel shows the data, before the model smooths it. The mean panel shows the average estimate. The sd panel shows the uncertainty. A high sd shows where the data do not fix the value. The probability panel shows how likely it is that rr is above 1 in each area. A cross marks each area where this probability is above 95% (1 of 30). The grey lines join the 49 pairs of neighbours. Small areas with few data often have extreme observed values; the model pulls them towards their neighbours or the average. Grey areas have no value.
sci.area_map@1.0.0.title: Area map of rr

sci.ensemble@1.0.0.caption_plain: The thin lines are 40 draws from the model. Each line is one possible path of y along time. The shaded band is the 90% interval of all 60 draws. The thick line is the median. The dots are the actual values. 96% of the actual values are in the 90% band.
sci.ensemble@1.0.0.title: Ensemble of y

sci.field_map@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each panel shows one statistic of intensity for each cell, from 80 draws of the posterior. The mean panel shows the average value. The sd panel shows the uncertainty. A high sd shows where the data do not fix the value. Empty cells have no value.
sci.field_map@1.0.0.title: Field map of intensity

sci.image_residuals@1.0.0.caption_plain: The first two panels show the observed values of image and the mean of 100 predictive draws of image, on one colour scale. The residual is the observed value minus the mean. In red cells the observed value is higher than the model, in blue cells it is lower. The normalised residual divides the residual by the uncertainty of the model. The normalised residuals have an sd of 1.04 and 4% are outside ±2. If the model fits, the sd is near 1, about 5% are outside ±2 and the image shows no pattern.
sci.image_residuals@1.0.0.title: Residuals of image

sci.phylogeny@1.0.0.caption_plain: The tree shows how the 16 tips are related: two tips that join near the right share a recent ancestor. The colour of each tip is the mean of body_mass. The strip on the right shows the same mean as a dot with the 90% interval as a line, from 160 draws of the predictions. The open circles are the observed values. 100% of them are inside the interval. 3 tips have no observed value: their estimate comes from their relatives. The tips are the levels of species.
sci.phylogeny@1.0.0.title: Phylogeny of body_mass

sci.point_pattern@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each dot is one spot at the posterior mean of its position (x, y). There are 40 points. Each ellipse contains the true position with 90% probability (from 80 draws). A large ellipse shows that the position is not certain. The colours show group. The background shows the mean of render. The median sd of a coordinate is 0.01.
sci.point_pattern@1.0.0.title: Points of x and y

sci.power_spectrum@1.0.0.caption_plain: The line is the median of bandpower in each bin of ell, from 400 draws of posterior. The shaded bands are the 50% and 90% intervals. The dashed line is the theory curve theory_dl. The dots are the observed values with their error bars. 75% of the observed values are in the 90% band.
sci.power_spectrum@1.0.0.title: Spectrum of bandpower

sci.ppc_image_grid@1.0.0.caption_plain: The first panel shows the observed values of image. The other panels are 5 images of image from the posterior predictive. All panels use one colour scale. If the model fits, the observed image looks like one more draw: the same shapes, the same contrast and the same noise.
sci.ppc_image_grid@1.0.0.title: Predictive images of image

sci.profile_bands@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each line is the median of u along x for one t. Use the slider to show one t with its bands. The bands are the 50% and 90% intervals. The dots are the actual values. 95% of the actual values are in the 90% band.
sci.profile_bands@1.0.0.title: Profiles of u

sci.rose@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each sector of the rose covers 22.5 degrees. The bars show the number of the observed wind_dir in it. The thick radial lines show the 90% interval of the same number in data simulated by the model (100 draws of wind_dir), and the dark outline is its median. 81% of the bars end inside the interval: a bar that ends outside it shows a direction that the model gets wrong. Zero is at the top and the angles go clockwise; one turn is 360 degrees.
sci.rose@1.0.0.title: Rose of wind_dir

sci.swatches@1.0.0.caption_plain: Each square is the colour of one chip of chip_rgb. The first panel shows the observed colours. The mean panel shows the average colour over 80 draws of posterior. The 2 draw panels show possible colours from the model. Where they differ, the model is not sure of the colour. The mean colour is on average 10 units from the observed colour (sRGB, 0 to 255 per channel). Thicker borders show a higher p_mode. The squares are on the row × col map of the chips.
sci.swatches@1.0.0.title: Colours of chip_rgb

sci.vector_field@1.0.0.caption_plain: The colours show the length of the traction vector in each cell, from 60 draws of the model. The arrows on the mean panel show the mean direction. A longer arrow shows a larger mean vector. The sd panel shows where the data do not fix the length of the vector.
sci.vector_field@1.0.0.title: Vector field of traction
